assessment: subjective design judgment; not trademark clearance

concepts.name: Confluence
notes: Two separate arrivals
One shared bend
Aqua: the joined passage
concepts.story: Cobie and Evan take different paths into one shared practice.
concepts.impression: A compact, flowing junction with two open arrivals and one rounded return.
concepts.beauty: Unequal upper gestures balance a generous lower curve. The rounded ends soften the diagonal without losing its direction.
concepts.hidden: Trace either upper end: the two paths become the same material at the waist. They are origins, not two finished objects linked together.
concepts.specific: The two arrivals refer to Cobie and Evan; the shared lower passage is the new name, Covan. Their unequal trajectories express two distinct contributions without assigning roles to either person.
concepts.portability: The junction could represent collaboration elsewhere. Its name-origin reading and asymmetric return give it a Covan rationale; neither makes the silhouette legally exclusive.
concepts.aqua: The shared waist marks the passage where two sources become one identity. Both origins remain silver, so the accent does not privilege one person.
concepts.watch: The overall gesture may read as a lowercase y. Judge that association before relying on the origin story.
concepts.letters: No letter encoding is claimed. The two-origin structure carries the idea.

concepts.name: Common Ground
notes: A broad enclosing gesture
A second gesture turns inside it
Aqua: where the second origin takes shape
concepts.story: Two names find room inside one independent lab.
concepts.impression: A quiet nested form: a broad upper shelter and a shorter, turned inner gesture.
concepts.beauty: The two radii and unequal heights make a balanced, off-centre silhouette. A clear internal channel lets the forms breathe.
concepts.hidden: One origin defines the outside; the second turns inside it. Together they establish a shared space without becoming matching halves.
concepts.specific: Covan is a new name with room for both Cobie and Evan. The outside/inside relation describes co-authorship, not a corporate hierarchy.
concepts.portability: Enclosure is a transferable idea. The deliberate two-gesture reading supports the name story, but this direction relies more on repeated brand use than on a literal letter signature.
concepts.aqua: Aqua follows the inner turn: the point where the second gesture begins to complete the first.
concepts.watch: Some viewers may see a lowercase letter pair. The inner channel is the detail to compare at 16px.
concepts.letters: The shapes are not intended as a readable CE monogram.

concepts.name: Meeting Point
notes: Two bowed paths start independently
Their material joins at one off-centre waist
Aqua: the shared portion, not a third part
concepts.story: Two independent curves become a single centre of gravity.
concepts.impression: A sculpted, pinched form with a stable base and two open upper ends.
concepts.beauty: Concave sides and broad curved shoulders create tension without sharp tips. The central overlap makes a strong one-color silhouette.
concepts.hidden: Two bowed paths cross in shared material. Each can be traced from a different upper origin to the opposite side of the base.
concepts.specific: Two starting points refer to Cobie and Evan. The shared waist is Covan itself: a new structure formed from both, rather than a plus sign between two names.
concepts.portability: A crossing can also suggest partnership elsewhere. Here the curved, asymmetrical joining and name-origin mapping matter; the concept does not claim that every junction belongs to Covan.
concepts.aqua: The accent identifies the common portion of both contributions. Removing it leaves the joining fully visible.
concepts.watch: The silhouette has an abstract X / hourglass association. It should be judged as a shape before that secondary reading is explained.
concepts.letters: No hidden alphabet is required for this direction.

concepts.name: Countervoice
notes: C: the enclosing sweep, before the tilt
E: an incomplete rhythm of shared interior levels
The whole construction rotates together
concepts.story: The first letters of two names share one curved voice.
concepts.impression: A curled, oblique form with an open outer sweep and a compact returning lip.
concepts.beauty: A long enclosing curve contrasts with a short internal return. Tilting the construction reduces the appearance of typeset initials.
concepts.hidden: In the construction view, C is the enclosing stroke. An E-like rhythm appears where the return divides the interior into unequal levels; it is a suggestion, not a complete E glyph.
concepts.specific: The two strokes refer to the first letters of Cobie and Evan. They borrow the same counterspace instead of sitting beside each other as CE.
concepts.portability: The association is stronger for names beginning C and E, but it is still an abstract mark. The inner-return construction gives a specific naming route without proving uniqueness.
concepts.aqua: Aqua sits on the returning voice as it enters the shared enclosure. It identifies the fusion rather than spelling a colored E.
concepts.watch: The letter reading is less immediate than the curl. At small sizes, judge the large counter and opening rather than the E suggestion.
concepts.letters: C is structural; E is an incomplete counterform reading. No literal CE is overlaid.

concepts.name: Shared Counter
notes: C: the open inner counter around the fold
E: the inner ledge shares the outer upper and lower turns
The letters are counterform readings, not separate glyphs
concepts.story: Cobie and Evan share a counter, just as their names share Covan.
concepts.impression: A rounded chamber with one inward fold and a single quiet, squared foot.
concepts.beauty: The closed perimeter gives visual calm; the off-centre pocket prevents it from becoming a neutral ring. Broad strokes keep the interior useful at icon scale.
concepts.hidden: The open negative space wraps around the inner fold like a C. The fold borrows the top and bottom of the enclosure to suggest an E-like three-level structure.
concepts.specific: One letter is read in empty space and the other in the material around it: two names contribute to the same whole without two colored initials.
concepts.portability: The counterform reading depends on the Cobie/Evan story. Without it, the form may be read as a rounded d; the concept offers a name-based rationale, not an untransferable symbol.
concepts.aqua: The short inner fold is the shared counter’s focal point. It changes neither the outline nor the letter reading in monochrome.
concepts.watch: A lowercase d or speech-form association is possible. The meaning should add interest, not be needed to rescue that first impression.
concepts.letters: The C is negative space. The E is a shared-stroke suggestion, intentionally not a literal glyph.

concepts.name: Covan Ligature
notes: O: the rounded upper counter
V / N: the central interval and diagonal
C / A are suggestions, not five forced glyphs
concepts.story: One name is built from shared curves, counters and a single connecting stroke.
concepts.impression: A rounded ligature: two uprights joined by an oblique passage.
concepts.beauty: The curved shoulder tempers the diagonal. A firm baseline and open lower intervals give the compact form a stable rhythm.
concepts.hidden: The rounded counter supplies an O association; the diagonal and uprights supply N. A V-like interval appears between the uprights. C and A are not independently encoded.
concepts.specific: The construction studies the relationships inside COVAN rather than stacking five initials. O, V and N provide a discoverable subset of the name.
concepts.portability: This could suit another name sharing those letters. It is a partial Covan ligature, not a claim that five letters make a symbol impossible to reuse.
concepts.aqua: The small upper join identifies the meeting between the rounded framework and the connecting stroke.
concepts.watch: An n-like first reading is likely. The central counter must remain open at 16px; all-five-letter completeness is deliberately sacrificed.
concepts.letters: O / V / N suggested. C / A omitted to protect the silhouette.

concepts.name: Oblique Name
notes: C / O: an open elliptical envelope
N: the diagonal relationship of the return
V / A omitted rather than invented
concepts.story: Covan leaves its name open to the next useful product.
concepts.impression: An asymmetric oval fold with a deliberate opening and an oblique return.
concepts.beauty: The outer sweep carries most of the weight; a short inward fold gives the right side tension. The open edge avoids a sealed, heavy badge.
concepts.hidden: C and O are alternate readings of the open envelope. The return and outer side suggest an N-like diagonal relationship. V and A are not claimed as complete hidden letters.
concepts.specific: This is a partial C–O–N construction from COVAN, with openness standing for a parent name that can hold future work. It keeps the name’s framework rather than illustrating a product category.
concepts.portability: An open oval is not exclusively Covan. The diagonal return and partial name reading distinguish the concept’s rationale, but it needs brand use to become owned in people’s memory.
concepts.aqua: The fold where the outer form becomes the inner relation is accented: the moment a name becomes a system.
concepts.watch: The return can suggest a stylized letter before the full name. Avoid explaining V or A through imaginary construction lines.
concepts.letters: C / O / N suggested. V / A omitted rather than forced.

concepts.name: Raised Edge
notes: 凡: an ordinary continuous surface
高: the same material takes a more considered shape
Aqua: the turn where refinement happens
concepts.story: 高凡 gives an ordinary surface a more considered shape.
concepts.impression: A continuous, lifted edge with one generous pocket of negative space.
concepts.beauty: A straight starting edge becomes a broad, controlled curve. The result has motion without an arrowhead or an aggressive apex.
concepts.hidden: The lower plane is the ordinary starting point; the upper turn is the same material after refinement. Elevation happens through shaping, not upward-pointing symbolism.
concepts.specific: The interpretation comes directly from 高凡: elevating the ordinary. It describes practical ideas becoming useful products through engineering and care.
concepts.portability: Refinement is broadly applicable, but the 高 / 凡 interpretation is a direct bilingual connection to this brand’s name. It does not depend on reading Chinese characters in the shape.
concepts.aqua: Aqua marks the turn where the original surface takes its refined form.
concepts.watch: A leaf or folded-sheet association is possible. Keep the technical cut and broad surface if this direction advances.
concepts.letters: No literal Chinese characters or English letters are encoded.

concepts.name: Shared Grain
notes: Each contour can hold a separate product identity
Shared curvature and one baseline hold the family together
Aqua: one active product within the independent studio
concepts.story: Independent products grow from the same Covan practice.
concepts.impression: Three unequal curved contours, aligned by one baseline and one family of radii.
concepts.beauty: The contours step inward without becoming identical blocks. Open channels create a rhythm that remains readable in one color.
concepts.hidden: Each contour can stand as its own product. Their shared curvature and baseline establish the parent identity without recoloring every product to match it.
concepts.specific: Covan’s job is to hold independent apps, tools and experiments together. Three contours illustrate that relationship; they do not assert that the studio will always have exactly three products.
concepts.portability: This is the most philosophy-led, transferable direction in the set. Its specificity comes from Covan’s parent-brand role, not a hidden name claim; assess that tradeoff explicitly.
concepts.aqua: One contour is active while the surrounding system stays silver. It represents a product receiving attention, not a permanent brand hierarchy.
concepts.watch: The stepped curve can suggest a signal or fingerprint. The lack of a direct name signature is its main weakness.
concepts.letters: No letters are claimed. This explores the requested portfolio-system direction.

concepts.name: Revision Fold
notes: The outer sweep is one pass through a product
The return folds into the same work, rather than circling outside it
Aqua: learning changing the next version
concepts.story: At Covan, what a product teaches us becomes part of its next version.
concepts.impression: An uneven loop with a compact return folded into its interior.
concepts.beauty: A generous outer arc and a smaller inner curve create two scales of movement. The offset opening keeps it from becoming a regular ring.
concepts.hidden: The second passage returns into the work itself. It represents learning changing the product, not a path going endlessly around it.
concepts.specific: The open outer sweep echoes the C/O in Covan, while the internal return expresses an independent lab maintaining and improving its own products.
concepts.portability: Iteration is a shared software principle. The internal return and partial name echo support Covan’s practice, but this direction has a weaker naming claim than the two-origin concepts.
concepts.aqua: Aqua is the return where learning enters the next version. It is an integrated curve, not a separate terminal tile.
concepts.watch: A spiral or curled letter may be seen first. The offset fold must remain distinct from a loading-ring silhouette.
concepts.letters: Only a loose C / O echo is intended. No full monogram is claimed.
